Note::TexAccessor::refs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::refs() const

Extract Cross-Reference Targets¶

refs() extracts the required key argument from complete cross-reference commands. It recognizes \ref, \eqref, \autoref, \pageref, \nameref, \cref, \Cref, \vref, and \Vref, including starred forms such as \eqref*. Each token is the argument body without the command or outer braces.

The method inventories uses of anchors; labels inventories their definitions. Comparing the two at document scope supports unresolved-reference checks, while preserving duplicates and source order allows callers to retain usage frequency and first-use position. refs() itself does not resolve keys, enforce uniqueness, follow included files, or determine whether TeX executes a command in its surrounding context.

Matching is exact and balanced. Nested braces in a key are retained, whitespace between command and argument is accepted, and a doubled backslash, longer name such as \reference, or incomplete braced argument contributes no token. Optional arguments are not part of these supported call forms and are not skipped.

The returned TokenBatch stores flat Text tokens() and Int64 offsets(). Cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]); this retains lane ownership for scalar, vector, matrix, and rank-three receivers without padding. Undefined input returns undefined tokens and canonical offsets [0]. Defined non-Text input is rejected. Scanning and copying are linear in source and retained-key bytes.

Example 1: Reference Families, Stars, And Balanced Keys¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\ref{eq:{energy}} \eqref* {eq:two} \cref{sec:a})",
    R"(\Cref{sec:b} \vref{fig:a} \Vref{fig:b} \nameref{name:a})",
    R"(\\ref{escaped} \reference{long} \ref{unfinished)"});
const auto result = source.tex().refs();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[7], dim=1, numel=7, encoding=utf8)
["eq:{energy}", "eq:two", "sec:a", "sec:b", "fig:a", "fig:b", "name:a"]

The first key retains its nested braces. The escaped, longer, and unfinished forms do not create false targets.

Example 2: Preserve Per-Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 3, 7, 7]

The first cell owns three targets, the second owns four, and the malformed-only third cell owns an empty range.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().refs();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().refs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "refs Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
refs Int64: rejected
